1.explanation: 1. components.js – this file declares the set of languages Prism knows about. We must add an “apex” entry under components.languages (aliasing or requiring “java”) so Apex appears in the language list, and the loader will include prism-apex.js. 2. plugins/autoloader/prism-autoloader.js – the autoloader maintains a map of language aliases -> real IDs. We must add “apex”: “java” so calls to loadLanguages(‘apex’) resolve to the Java component. 3. gulpfile.js/paths.js – the build scripts enumerate which language files to bundle by default. We should add the new prism-apex.js to the main components array so that it’s automatically picked up by the build.
1.bug_scenario: The user wants to add first‐class support for the Salesforce Apex language to Prism. Apex is nearly identical to Java from a syntax/highlighting standpoint, so they’d like to alias it to the existing Java grammar. In the screenshot we see an Apex code snippet tagged “Apex” in a Prism code block and highlighted correctly (because it’s Java‐compatible), but Prism doesn’t recognize “apex”—it either treats it as an unknown language or falls back to Java and shows “Java” in its UI. We need to teach Prism that “apex” is a valid language ID (alias for “java”), allow the autoloader to resolve it, and include it in the build.
